final_answer:
Cause: load_config did a shallow copy of DEFAULTS (dict(DEFAULTS)), so nested dicts like logging and allowed_hosts were shared with the defaults; merge() also mutated its base in place and inserted override lists/dicts by reference. So enable_debug() changing a returned config (appending "file" to logging.handlers, "127.0.0.1" to allowed_hosts) leaked into the defaults and later configs.

Fix: merge() now returns a new deep-copied dict without mutating either input, and load_config passes DEFAULTS straight into it (no shared state). Existing tests pass (4/4). I did not add a regression test for the leak; modes.py was left unchanged since the fix is in the loader/merge path.
